Job Description:
About the job
We are looking for an experienced Senior Data Engineer to join a leading organization and play a key role in designing, building and supporting scalable data engineering solutions.
This is a hands-on senior role where Python, SQL and AWS are critical, with responsibility for production-ready data pipelines, cloud data platforms, engineering standards and technical guidance.
CORE TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Strong hands-on Python experience – essential
Advanced SQL experience – essential
Strong hands-on AWS experience – essential
Proven experience delivering production-ready data pipelines and data platforms
Strong understanding of data modelling, data warehousing and analytics-oriented schemas
Experience with batch and incremental data processing
Experience ingesting data from relational databases, cloud storage, APIs and file-based sources
Experience with Git, CI/CD and automation
Experience working within Agile or SAFe environments
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Design and implement scalable data ingestion and transformation pipelines across multiple systems and data domains.
Build robust batch and incremental processing solutions.
Implement appropriate error handling, monitoring, alerting, validation and reconciliation.
Design data solutions aligned to data platform strategy and target architecture.
Contribute to the evolution of a cloud-based, AWS-aligned data environment.
Assess solutions for security, performance, cost and supportability.
Review data engineering code and configurations and contribute to engineering standards and best practices.
Optimise existing pipelines and data models to improve performance, reliability and maintainability.
Apply version control, automated testing, CI/CD and structured release practices.
Provide technical guidance and coaching to less experienced Data Engineers.
Collaborate with Analytics, BI, Data Science, Product and business stakeholders.
Support operational readiness, monitoring, incident resolution and root cause analysis.
Build solutions with appropriate data security, privacy, access control and governance considerations.
Maintain technical documentation covering pipelines, data models and operational requirements.
Contribute to Agile ceremonies, sprint planning, estimation, prioritisation and continuous improvement.
Identify practical opportunities to use approved AI tooling across data engineering, including pipeline analysis, optimisation, testing, documentation and data exploration.
Validate AI-assisted outputs and ensure their use remains aligned with security and governance requirements.
REQUIREMENTS
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related discipline.
4–7+ years of professional experience in Data Engineering or related roles.
Strong Python, SQL and AWS experience.
Demonstrated experience delivering production-ready data pipelines and platforms.
Strong foundation in data modelling and data warehousing principles.
Experience working within Agile or SAFe delivery environments.
Experience using AI tooling within engineering workflows.
Practical experience applying AI to support data pipeline understanding, optimisation, testing or documentation.
Understanding of responsible AI use and validation of AI-assisted outputs.
Familiarity with analytics and BI tools such as Power BI.
Experience coaching or guiding other engineers.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills.
Understanding of data security, privacy, governance and engineering risk.

Our mandate
The Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited (IDC) was established in 1940 by an Act of Parliament (Industrial Development Corporation Act, No. 22 of 1940) and is fully owned by the South African Government.

The IDC was mandated to develop domestic industrial capacity, specifically in manufactured goods, to mitigate the disruption of trade between Europe and South Africa during the Second World War.

We have contributed to the implementation of South Africa's industrial policy for more than 70 years and established, among others, the petro-chemicals and minerals beneficiation industries. We have stimulated large industrial projects in these industries - acknowledged today as the cornerstones of the country's manufacturing sector - and influenced the establishment of industries in fabricated metals, agriculture and clothing and textiles.

During the 1990s, our mandate was expanded to include investment in the rest of Africa. The Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique was the first such venture. We secured investors from around the globe to establish a major industrial enterprise in a country plagued by decades of civil war. The smelter illustrated the viability of large projects on a continent often shunned by investors. Currently, our investments in Africa include mining, agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications.

The IDC's funding is generated through income from loan and equity investments and exits from mature investments, as well as borrowings from commercial banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and other lenders.

We align our priorities with government's policy direction and remain committed to developing the country's industrial capacity, as well as playing a major role in facilitating job creation through industrialisation.
Our industrial development role
As a key implementing agency of industrial policy, the IDC's activities currently centre on the National Development Plan (NDP), the New Growth Path (NGP) and the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP). We identify sector development opportunities aligned with policy objectives and develop projects in partnership with stakeholders.

By developing industrial capacity the IDC achieves specific outcomes. The most important of these is to enable job creation through the companies we fund. In addition, IDC funding continues to promote regional development and integration, economic empowerment of communities and growing black industrialists. The IDC remains committed to promoting environmentally sustainable growth and increasing sectoral diversity to boost the local production of goods. The corporation also plays a critical role, directly and through its sefa subsidiary, in promoting entrepreneurial development and growing the SME sector.

While our funding activities focus mainly on the private sector, we work closely with different levels of government agencies and sector organisations to coordinate industry development. We also support government in other areas related to its development objectives, such as research and management of government funds allocated to achieving specific outcomes. We pro-actively develop and implement strategies in the rest of Africa to create and integrate value chains across the continent. Our aim is to use the strengths of different countries in the region to establish a more competitive industrial base.

We have stimulated large industrial projects in these industries - acknowledged today as the cornerstones of the country's manufacturing sector - and influenced the establishment of industries in fabricated metals, agriculture and clothing and textiles.

Currently, our investments in Africa include mining, agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications.

The IDC's funding is generated through income from loan and equity investments and exits from mature investments, as well as borrowings from commercial banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and other lenders.

We have contributed to the implementation of South Africa's industrial policy for more than 70 years and established, among others, the petro-chemicals and minerals beneficiation industries. We have stimulated large industrial projects in these industries - acknowledged today as the cornerstones of the country's manufacturing sector - and influenced the establishment of industries in fabricated metals, agriculture and clothing and textiles.

During the 1990s, our mandate was expanded to include investment in the rest of Africa. The Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique was the first such venture. We secured investors from around the globe to establish a major industrial enterprise in a country plagued by decades of civil war. The smelter illustrated the viability of large projects on a continent often shunned by investors. Currently, our investments in Africa include mining, agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications.

The IDC's funding is generated through income from loan and equity investments and exits from mature investments, as well as borrowings from commercial banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and other lenders.

We align our priorities with government's policy direction and remain committed to developing the country's industrial capacity, as well as playing a major role in facilitating job creation through industrialisation.
Our industrial development role
As a key implementing agency of industrial policy, the IDC's activities currently centre on the National Development Plan (NDP), the New Growth Path (NGP) and the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP). We identify sector development opportunities aligned with policy objectives and develop projects in partnership with stakeholders.

By developing industrial capacity the IDC achieves specific outcomes. The most important of these is to enable job creation through the companies we fund. In addition, IDC funding continues to promote regional development and integration, economic empowerment of communities and growing black industrialists. The IDC remains committed to promoting environmentally sustainable growth and increasing sectoral diversity to boost the local production of goods. The corporation also plays a critical role, directly and through its sefa subsidiary, in promoting entrepreneurial development and growing the SME sector.

While our funding activities focus mainly on the private sector, we work closely with different levels of government agencies and sector organisations to coordinate industry development. We also support government in other areas related to its development objectives, such as research and management of government funds allocated to achieving specific outcomes. We pro-actively develop and implement strategies in the rest of Africa to create and integrate value chains across the continent. Our aim is to use the strengths of different countries in the region to establish a more competitive industrial base.

Job Title: Project Manager: Education Programmes - Tirisano Construction Fund
Job Description:
Synopsis
A position exists within the Tirisano Construction Fund (TCF) team for an accomplished and competent Project Manager – Education Programmes. This position will be based on a three-year (36 month) performance-based fixed-term contract, through the IDC.
Background of the Tirisano Construction Fund
Seven Construction Companies entered a Settlement Agreement with the South African government to establish the Tirisano Construction Fund. The Fund is constituted as a Trust and the Trustees are designated by seven construction companies and Government, plus a Trustee from SAFCEC - as outlined in the Settlement Agreement.
The Settlement Agreement stipulates that the construction companies should collectively contribute R1.5 billion over 12 years (an average of R125 million per annum). The funds will be used for social and economic benefit to the construction industry, in seven programmes as follows:
Enterprise Development Programme (EDP): the development and promotion of construction firms owned and managed by Black People through, for example, providing working capital at concessional rates;
Engineering Bursaries Programme (EBP): providing bursaries to previously disadvantaged persons studying engineering, building science or quantity surveying at a tertiary institution, principally based on mentorship programs guaranteeing future employment for such previously disadvantaged persons in the Construction Companies, to the extent feasible at the time;
Construction Occupations Development Programme (CODP): providing bursaries to previously disadvantaged persons being trained as artisans and/or the equivalent level of construction occupations, principally based on mentorship programs guaranteeing future employment for such previously disadvantaged persons in the Construction Companies, to the extent feasible at the time;
Basic Education Programme (BEP): supporting and enhancing mathematics and science education at public schools;
Social Infrastructure Programme (SIP): promoting social and economic welfare, including funding social infrastructure build programs for student accommodation, health clinics, rural bridges and sports fields at public schools;
Technical Capacity Programme (TCP): funding the appointment of professionals to provide the Government with engineering, project management and other services that assist the Government (and local government), and strengthen its capacity, to design, construct, operate and maintain public infrastructure through, amongst others, the secondment of skilled personnel from organisations operating in RSA; and
Professionalising Engineering Practitioners Programme (PEPP): through funding the relevant training academies and/or mentoring institutions which provide a structured development program for graduate engineers, to facilitate such engineers' registration by the Engineering Council of South Africa as "professional engineers" in terms of the Engineering Profession Act No. 46 of 2000.
Job Description
MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
TCF Partners and Programme Management
Manage day-to-day operations with implementing partners delivering TCF education and skills programmes.
Ensure partners deliver against signed agreements, workplans, budgets, and agreed milestones.
Conduct regular site visits and partner engagements to assess quality of implementation and learner/student experience.
Provide technical and operational support to partners to strengthen delivery, including special interventions from TCF from time to time.
Identify and manage programme risks, escalating issues timeously with proposed mitigation plans.
Implement approved strategies for TCF’s education programmes.
Financial Management
Manage disbursement of funds to partners in line with grant agreements and TCF finance policies.
Support the Fund Administrator in facilitating payments to beneficiaries, bursary holders, and implementing partners, including coordinating internal IDC financial reporting and obtaining the required approvals and signatures.
Review and verify partner budgets, cash flow forecasts, and expenditure reports.
Monitors spend against budget, flag variances, and ensure funds are used for intended purposes.
Support annual budgeting and forecasting for the education portfolio.
Ensure partner financial reports meet audit and compliance requirements.
Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting
Implement and maintain M&E frameworks and identifying impact areas for both programmes, tracking outputs, outcomes and impact indicators
Assess monthly partner reports against programme implementation targets and follow up on performance gaps or required corrective action.
Collect, verify, and analyse data from partners; maintain accurate programme records and databases.
Support Senior Management on projects FICA processes within the IDC.
Compile, prepare and submit monthly project reports, annual report stories and interview inputs, in addition to general TCF management reports.
Track progress against multiyear programme targets and recommend course corrections
Commission or support external evaluations and use findings to inform programme design.
Strategic and Stakeholder Engagement
Contribute to TCF programme strategy, design, and continuous improvement based on evidence and sector best practice.
Support due diligence and selection of new implementing partners for TCF programmes.
Attend to beneficiary and bursary-holder queries, coordinate planned support programmes, and facilitate correspondence with university bursary offices.
Governance and Compliance
Ensure all programmes comply with relevant legislation, funder requirements, and internal policies (including B-BBEE/skills development alignment where relevant) Maintain proper documentation for grant agreements, compliance checks, and reporting audit trails.
Qualification and Experience
QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in education or Social Sciences or Development Studies or Commerce or Engineering and Built environment, or related fields.
KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Minimum 5 - 8 years' experience managing education or development programmes, including experience with multiyear, multi-partner initiatives.
Demonstrated experience in transformational/development programmes targeting Quintile 1 - 3 schools or historically disadvantaged communities.
Experience managing bursary or scholarship programmes advantageous.
Proven financial management experience.
Experience in monitoring, evaluation, and donor/funder reporting. Experience working with corporate social investment (CSI), foundation, NGO, or development sector funding models.
Roles and Responsibilities
TECHNICAL/FUNCTIONAL COMPETENCIES
Strong financial acumen and budget management skills.
Excellent partner/stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.
Strong M&E and data analysis skills; comfortable working with education/impact data.
Excellent written, verbal reporting skills and presentation skills.
Project management skills: planning, risk management, multi-stakeholder coordination.
Understanding of the South African education system, STEM pipeline challenges, and the engineering/construction skills landscape.
Cultural competence and commitment to equity and transformation in education.
Proficient in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint).
Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel to partner and programme sites.
Roles and Responsibilities (cont.)
BEHAVIOURAL COMPETENCIES
Strong systems thinking and analytical capability.
High professional integrity and governance ethics.
Strong communication and facilitation skills.
Ability to work in a high‑structure environment with defined deliverables.
Commitment to contractor development and sector transformation.
Independent, disciplined and delivery‑focused.

Job Title: Senior Manager: Enterprise Development Programme (EDP) - Tirisano Construction Fund

The EDP Senior Manager is accountable for the end-to-end management and continued development of TCF’s Enterprise Development Programme across Bid Windows; new, active and legacy portfolios. The role integrates programme strategy and governance, programme entry and funding, contractor development, loan and portfolio management, recovery and legal matters, and programme reporting and financial control.
Operating within a small TCF team, the EDP Senior Manager is expected to combine senior judgement and governance accountability with hands-on portfolio control and delivery. The Senior Manager leads the Primary Specialist and Targeted Specialist resources, coordinates appropriate support from the TCF Administrator and other IDC/TCF functions, and establishes fit-for-purpose systems, processes and support arrangements as the programme evolves.
Job Description
MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Programme Strategy, Governance & Development
Own and implement the EDP strategy, operating model, annual priorities, governance framework, controls, budget and programme performance.
Translate TCF decisions into practical programme action; maintain an integrated view of portfolio performance, risk, resources and emerging priorities.
Develop and refine programme systems, procedures, templates, controls and improvement initiatives using implementation experience and lessons learned.
Programme Entry, Evaluation & Funding
Lead EDP Bid Window 5 implementation.
Coordinate multidisciplinary assessments, site and specialist inputs, risk evaluation, funding recommendations, approval documentation, contracting, conditions precedent, onboarding and disbursement readiness.
Ensure evaluation and funding decisions are properly documented, defensible and implemented in accordance with approved mandates and governance requirements.
Contractor Development, Project Performance & Specialist Support
Maintain effective oversight of participating contractors, supported by the Primary Specialist as the principal contractor-facing professional resource.
Review contractor project, commercial, operational and capability performance; identify material risks, development needs, PIP actions and required interventions.
Appoint, direct and manage Primary and Targeted Specialist resources within approved scopes, budgets and deliverables; assess the quality and effectiveness of specialist interventions.
Loan Portfolio Monitoring & Financial Risk

Develop and maintain appropriate portfolio dashboards, risk and action records; investigate exceptions and determine follow-up, intervention or escalation.
Coordinate routine SAP/Finance information and administrative support through the TCF Administrator and relevant IDC functions, while retaining responsibility for analysis, reconciliation and action.

Relevant professional registration or recognised professional membership will be an advantage.

Our mandate
The Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited (IDC) was established in 1940 by an Act of Parliament (Industrial Development Corporation Act, No. 22 of 1940) and is fully owned by the South African Government.

The IDC was mandated to develop domestic industrial capacity, specifically in manufactured goods, to mitigate the disruption of trade between Europe and South Africa during the Second World War.

We have contributed to the implementation of South Africa's industrial policy for more than 70 years and established, among others, the petro-chemicals and minerals beneficiation industries. We have stimulated large industrial projects in these industries - acknowledged today as the cornerstones of the country's manufacturing sector - and influenced the establishment of industries in fabricated metals, agriculture and clothing and textiles.

During the 1990s, our mandate was expanded to include investment in the rest of Africa. The Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique was the first such venture. We secured investors from around the globe to establish a major industrial enterprise in a country plagued by decades of civil war. The smelter illustrated the viability of large projects on a continent often shunned by investors. Currently, our investments in Africa include mining, agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications.

The IDC's funding is generated through income from loan and equity investments and exits from mature investments, as well as borrowings from commercial banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and other lenders.

We align our priorities with government's policy direction and remain committed to developing the country's industrial capacity, as well as playing a major role in facilitating job creation through industrialisation.
Our industrial development role
As a key implementing agency of industrial policy, the IDC's activities currently centre on the National Development Plan (NDP), the New Growth Path (NGP) and the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP). We identify sector development opportunities aligned with policy objectives and develop projects in partnership with stakeholders.

By developing industrial capacity the IDC achieves specific outcomes. The most important of these is to enable job creation through the companies we fund. In addition, IDC funding continues to promote regional development and integration, economic empowerment of communities and growing black industrialists. The IDC remains committed to promoting environmentally sustainable growth and increasing sectoral diversity to boost the local production of goods. The corporation also plays a critical role, directly and through its sefa subsidiary, in promoting entrepreneurial development and growing the SME sector.

While our funding activities focus mainly on the private sector, we work closely with different levels of government agencies and sector organisations to coordinate industry development. We also support government in other areas related to its development objectives, such as research and management of government funds allocated to achieving specific outcomes. We pro-actively develop and implement strategies in the rest of Africa to create and integrate value chains across the continent. Our aim is to use the strengths of different countries in the region to establish a more competitive industrial base.

The Retail Coordinator provides administrative, operational and reporting support to the retail business, ensuring that retail activities, store support requirements, stock processes, launches, promotions, incentives and communication flows are coordinated accurately and on time.
The role supports the National Retail Sales & Operations Manager, Area Managers, Store Managers and Retail Sales Teams by maintaining trackers, consolidating information, following up on outstanding actions, coordinating retail administration and ensuring that accurate records are available to support decision-making and execution.
The Retail Coordinator is a key support role that helps keep the retail function organised, compliant and execution-ready by assisting with communication, documentation, reporting, stock and POS coordination, launch support, incentive administration and day-to-day follow-through across the retail network.
Key responsibilities include:
Retail Administration, Coordination and Communication
Coordinate day-to-day retail administration, ensuring accurate records, trackers and supporting documents are maintained and updated.
Support the Retail Manager and Area Managers with follow-ups, meeting notes, action trackers and deadline monitoring.
Prepare and distribute clear retail communications, reminders, updates and required information to Area Managers, Store Managers and Retail Sales Teams.
Assist with the coordination of retail meetings, training sessions, launches, events and operational activities.
Follow up on outstanding information, incomplete submissions and required documentation to ensure deadlines are met.
Coordinate and place office stationery orders, maintain accurate records and ensure supplies are available to support day-to-day operations.
Maintain organised electronic folders and records for retail activities, store support, submissions, incentives, launches and reporting.
Complete and oversee basic sales administration required to support the effective operation of the Core division.
Retail Operations Support
Support the implementation of retail standards, operational procedures, customer-experience requirements and compliance processes across stores.
Assist with the preparation, updating and circulation of store checklists, operational tools, scorecards and templates.
Coordinate information required for new store openings, closures, refits, events and operational projects.
Track store support requests, operational gaps, action plans and follow-up items until completion.
Take responsibility for the Woolworths self-service locations by ensuring shelves are adequately stocked and maintaining clear communication with the relevant in-store teams.
Help ensure that retail teams receive the correct information, forms, documentation and support needed to execute in-store requirements.
Oversee the administration and day-to-day operation of the Student Store, including stock management, ordering, invoicing, customer and account administration, and coordination with relevant internal teams.
Stock, POS, Launch and Promotion Coordination
Coordinate weekly stock-count information and follow up on missing, late or incomplete stock feedback from stores.
Maintain trackers for stock gaps, expired stock, testers, samples, professional products, consumables and relevant store support orders.
Assist with support orders for launches, promotions, events and store requirements, ensuring information is submitted accurately and within agreed timelines.
Support POS retail setup and maintenance administration, including campaign and discount loading, new staff setup, product loading and related update requests.
Assist with launch and promotion preparation by coordinating store requirements, communication, support material and follow-up reporting.
Track campaign, promotion and incentive information to support accurate execution and reporting.
Support the implementation and administration of Core division promotions, campaigns, launches and commercial initiatives.
Stakeholder and Retail Team Support
Provide reliable administrative support to the Retail Manager, Area Managers, Store Managers, internal teams and relevant external stakeholders.
Coordinate requests between Retail, Marketing, Education, Finance, HR, Planning and other departments to support smooth execution.
Ensure agreed information, updates and documentation are shared with the correct stakeholders timeously.
Assist with resolving general retail queries by gathering information, directing requests appropriately and following up until closure.
Support the preparation of weekly retail updates, meeting packs, presentation information and communication summaries.
Support Regional Managers with new door account openings and related administrative requirements, ensuring required information and documentation is gathered, processed and followed up.
People, Training and Team Administration Support
Maintain retail team contact lists, role information, store allocations and relevant staff administration trackers.
Support the scheduling and coordination of training sessions, meetings, team check-ins and retail initiatives.
Assist with the collection and consolidation of attendance, training completion, roster-related information and other people-related retail administration.
Follow up on outstanding submissions from retail teams and escalate repeated non-compliance to the Retail Manager or relevant Area Manager.
Complete and submit payroll documentation accurately and on time, including the recording and verification of overtime hours.
Help maintain clear records of team incentives, recognition programmes, communication updates and engagement activities.
Market, Store and Competitor Information Support
Assist with the collection and consolidation of store, competitor, mall and customer-experience feedback received from Area Managers and retail teams.
Maintain trackers for competitor activity, store opportunities, trade challenges and recurring operational themes.
Prepare summaries of key observations, risks and opportunities for review by the Retail Manager.
Ensure supporting photos, feedback forms, visit notes and other evidence are stored and organised for future reference.
Reporting, Trackers and Performance Administration
Maintain accurate weekly and monthly retail trackers covering sales updates, store feedback, stock concerns, incentives, expenses, consumables, launches, events and operational actions.
Consolidate information received from Area Managers and stores into clear summaries for review by the Retail Manager.
Check submissions for completeness, accuracy and consistency, and follow up where information is missing or unclear.
Prepare reporting packs, dashboards, meeting notes and action logs using Excel, PowerPoint, Word and other agreed tools.
Track deadlines, owners and completion status for actions arising from store visits, meetings, audits, performance reviews and operational checks.
Support incentive administration by maintaining point trackers, checking supporting information, preparing updates and assisting with results communication.
Process invoices from the student store to the relevant customer accounts using Syspro, ensuring supporting information is complete and accurate.
Maintain accurate Student Store records and ensure all transactions, invoices and supporting documentation are processed correctly.
Monitor Student Store sales and stock levels and provide regular reporting, insights and follow-up actions to management.
Complete basic sales administration and reporting requirements for assigned regions and portfolios, including follow-up on incomplete or outstanding submissions.
Complete ad hoc reconciliations for the Sales team, investigate discrepancies and provide supporting documentation where required.
Monitor retail costs such as event support, consumables, samples, testers and other approved support requirements, and prepare information for Finance review when needed.
Continuously improve administrative processes, trackers and filing systems to reduce duplication, improve accuracy and support faster follow-through.
Core Competencies:
Plans, Organises and Follows Through: Manages multiple tasks, deadlines and priorities accurately and reliably.
Strong Administration and Attention to Detail: Maintains accurate records, trackers, reports and supporting documentation.
Communicates Clearly and Professionally: Shares information in a clear, timely and appropriate manner with retail teams and stakeholders.
Builds Collaborative Relationships: Works effectively with Area Managers, Store Managers and internal departments to support execution.
Demonstrates Accountability: Takes ownership of assigned tasks, follows up on outstanding actions and escalates risks when needed.
Uses Data and Systems Confidently: Works accurately with spreadsheets, reports, dashboards and retail information systems.
Adapts to Changing Priorities: Remains organised and calm when retail priorities, deadlines or business needs change.
Supports Excellence in Execution: Helps ensure that retail plans, launches, promotions and operational activities are completed properly and on time.
Qualifications and Experience:
Relevant qualification in Business Administration, Retail Management, Sales, Marketing or a related field is advantageous.
Minimum two to three years’ experience in retail administration, sales support, operations coordination or a similar support role.
Experience in a retail, skincare, cosmetics or customer-facing environment is advantageous.
Strong administrative, organisational and follow-up skills.
Good understanding of retail operations, stock processes, promotions, reporting and store support requirements.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Confident working knowledge of Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook; experience with trackers, dashboards and reporting templates is essential.
Ability to work independently, manage competing deadlines and maintain accuracy under pressure.

Job Description:
Purpose of role:
The Replication Administrator is responsible for the independent, end-to-end administration of replicated fund mandates — ingesting and processing 3rd party trade and cash data, striking an independently derived NAV, performing full fund accounting, and producing client-specific reporting. The role exists to give clients an independent check on their primary administrator, not simply to mirror data received from a 3rd party, and is central to meeting daily, weekly and monthly client SLAs across an allocated book of funds
Duties and responsibilities:
Daily Processing
Receive and validate 3rd party trade and cash files (ASISA and non-ASISA formats) for all allocated funds.
Capture and process trades and cash transactions accurately and within daily cut-off times.
Investigate and resolve breaks, pricing exceptions, and reconciliation discrepancies between the replicated book and 3rd party data.
Escalate unresolved data or file-format issues to the relevant fund accountant, 3rd party administrator, or ICT support.
Weekly / Monthly Processing
Perform independent NAV striking for allocated funds, applying the correct valuation policy, pricing sources, and corporate actions.
Calculate and process management, performance, trustee and other fees and expense accruals accurately.
Prepare and self-review the full trial balance and supporting valuation working papers ahead of client and investor deadlines.
Investigate and correct any variances between the replicated NAV and the primary administrator's NAV, documenting explanations for material differences.
Client Reporting
Produce client-specific reporting packs, including exact replicas of segregated mandate monthly PDF valuation packs, to the agreed format and deadline.
Conduct a thorough self-review of all fee calculations and reports prior to client submission — no report should be sent without independent review.
Respond to client and 3rd party queries on valuations, fees and reporting in a professional and timely manner.
Fund Onboarding & Change
Support the onboarding of new local and offshore funds onto the replication administration platform, including non-ASISA source formats.
Contribute to testing and sign-off of process or system changes (e.g. automation of file ingestion) affecting the replication administration function.
Maintain up-to-date process documentation for all funds administered.
Risk, Control & Governance
Adhere to all SLA, compliance, and internal control requirements applicable to the replication administration function.
Maintain a complete and accurate audit trail for all trades, cash, fee calculations, and NAV adjustments.
Proactively flag operational risks, control gaps, or recurring errors to the Team Leader / Ops Manager
Required experience:
Relevant tertiary qualification (e.g. B.Com, Finance, Accounting, or equivalent) preferred.
2 years' experience in fund/hedge fund administration, fund accounting, or investment operations.
Working knowledge of ASISA reporting standards and unit trust / hedge fund valuation principles advantageous.
Experience with fund accounting or portfolio management systems advantageous.
Key competencies:
Strong attention to detail and a self-review, quality-first mindset.
Sound understanding of fund accounting, NAV calculation, and fee/expense processing.
Ability to manage multiple funds, deadlines, and stakeholders concurrently.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in reconciling and explaining valuation variances.
Clear written and verbal communication for client-facing reporting and query resolution.
Comfortable working with data across varied file formats and adapting to process/system change.
Key Performance Areas:
Performance in this role is assessed against the Replication Administration role scorecard, including but not limited to:
Providing end-to-end services in the daily, weekly and monthly processes involved in servicing allocated funds and their investment managers.
Accuracy and timeliness of NAV striking, fee calculations, and client reporting.
Consistently meeting client SLAs, with evidenced self-review prior to client submission.
Successful onboarding of new funds within agreed timelines.

Job Description:
Position Overview:
We are hiring a Business Analyst to play a key role in the implementation and ongoing management of Sonata One's solutions for our clients.
This is an internally focused role within our Implementation team, responsible for how Sonata One itself operates. The BA is responsible for design, documentation and improving our internal processes, so that every service line runs in a consistent, controlled and scalable way. This includes working alongside our learning and development team ensuring our people are trained to deliver those processes well.
This is a varied role sitting at the intersection of implementation, operations, CRM and technology. You will work directly with our internal stakeholders, namely the technology and operations function to understand their requirements, processes and objectives, translating these into clear business requirements and actionable plans.
This is a critical role to the scaling and success of Sonata One. We are transforming into a larger business which requires structure at all levels. You will be a trusted internal advisor, helping senior members of the team understand how Sonata One works, identifying and opportunities to improve processes and ensuring that implementations are delivered effectively.
The role will suit someone who is structured, logical, enjoys working with people, asking questions, understanding how businesses operate and turning complex requirements into clear, structured solutions.
Responsibilities
Process Mapping
Map current-state processes across service lines: Subscription, KYC/AML, Tax, Transfer Agency and investor portal
Understand and identify the gaps that exist in our existing processes, specifically between teams and the interplay between functions
Design target state processes that are standardised, efficient and scalable. We operate as one global team and do not necessarily need different procedures for different jurisdictions
Revamp and maintain our central process library: process maps, standard operating procedures, guides, and policies, including any newly developed documentation.
Working with the implementation manager to define an effective client lifecycle. Map workflow from business development to Implementation and ongoing BAU
Build strong relationships with client stakeholders and act as a key point of contact throughout implementation projects
Gather, document and analyse business and functional requirements
Translate internal requirements into clear actions, processes and deliverables for internal teams, specifically technology and operation
Identify dependencies, risks, issues and potential blockers and work collaboratively to resolve them
Gap analysis and continuous improvement
Find gaps, bottlenecks, manual workarounds and control weaknesses in how we operate today.
Prioritise improvements by impact, risk and effort, and build the business case where investment is needed.
Track improvement initiatives through to delivery and measure the benefits.
Turn feedback from client implementations, passed on by the external BA, into internal fixes.
Internal training and enablement
Work with the learning and development lead to design and deliver training for Sonata One staff on processes, systems and controls.
Build onboarding pathways for new joiners in each team
Check understanding and adherence through refreshers and spot checks, in partnership with team leads
Technology and data
Work with the externally facing BA to define requirements for system enhancements, and automation
Work with technology and product teams on testing and roll-out of internal changes
Support management information (MI) and KPI reporting on process performance.
Business Analysis
Facilitate workshops, meetings and discovery sessions with internal stakeholders
Work with the CTO, Head of Product, Director Of Operations and MD of Growth to establish business priorities for any system changes required to deliver
Map and document current-state and future-state processes
Translate business requirements into clear and actionable documentation
Ensure requirements are understood consistently across clients, Implementation, Operations, CRM and Technology
Experience Required:
Experience working as a Business Analyst in an operational, process improvement or business transformation environment
Proven experience mapping, redesigning and documenting internal processes, ideally across multiple teams or service lines
Strong understanding of change delivery and the ability to manage multiple improvement initiatives and priorities at once
Experience working with internal stakeholders, including operations, compliance and technology teams
Ability to understand complex operational processes and turn them into clear process maps, and training materials
Comfortable working with team leads and senior stakeholders, and bringing people along through process change
Ability to balance the needs of individual teams with consistency, control and scalability across the wider business
Strong understanding of:
Business analysis methodologies and techniques, including translating complex requirements into practical steps
Client implementation and onboarding
Process mapping and process improvement
Stakeholder management and client communication
Technology-enabled business processes
Financial services or fintech environments
Experience within fintech or financial services is important for this position, particularly where candidates have worked with regulated environments, complex client onboarding or technology-enabled financial processes. Experience within private markets, fund administration, investor onboarding or adjacent financial services environments would be advantageous.
Personal Attributes
Highly client-focused, with a genuine desire to understand and solve client problems
Naturally curious and comfortable asking questions to get to the root of an issue
Strong communicator who can build relationships with both clients and internal stakeholders
Highly organised with strong attention to detail
Comfortable managing multiple projects, priorities and stakeholders simultaneously
Commercially aware and able to understand the wider impact of decisions
Confident challenging existing processes and suggesting better ways of working
Proactive, solutions-focused and comfortable working in an environment where things are continually evolving
Collaborative and willing to work across functions to get things done
Hungry to learn, develop and make an impact within a growing business

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Technology or a related field preferred but not essential with relevant experience
Business Analysis, Project Management or related professional qualifications are advantageous

Job Description:
Job Overview
To execute the daily data collection, compilation and analysis that powers the contracted analytics services at the core of Vontier's end-to-end mining solutions. The role is the operational backbone of the analytics service delivery: ensuring the data underpinning customer-facing insight is accurate, validated, reconciled on time, and free of unmanaged exceptions.
Mining customers rely on these analytics as a cornerstone of the solutions deployed to them, so the integrity, timeliness and defensibility of the data directly determine service quality and customer trust. The role combines disciplined day-to-day execution with analytical rigour, identifying trends, managing exceptions, and producing reporting that turns raw operational data into reliable, actionable insight.
Responsibilities
Data collection and compilation
Execute daily collection and compilation of operational data feeding the contracted analytics services.
Ensure data completeness, accuracy and consistency across all sources.
Manage data intake from multiple systems, sites and customer feeds.
Validation and reconciliation
Validate data integrity, applying quality checks and controls before analysis and reporting.
Complete reconciliations accurately and on time, in line with contractual and service commitments.
Identify, investigate and manage exceptions, anomalies and discrepancies to resolution.
Escalate unresolved or material issues to the Senior Manager promptly.
Analysis and reporting
Analyse data to identify trends, patterns and outliers relevant to customer operations and contract performance.
Produce accurate, timely analytics outputs and reports for customers and internal stakeholders.
Translate data findings into clear, meaningful insight supporting customer decision-making.
Support continuous improvement of analytics methods, controls and reporting.
Service delivery support
Ensure analytics service delivery meets SLA, accuracy and timeliness requirements.
Maintain documentation of data processes, controls and reconciliations for audit and compliance.
Required Skills / Qualifications / Certifications / Tech Stack
Essential
4+ years in a data analyst, operations analyst or reporting analyst role, ideally in mining, industrial, telematics or data-services contexts.
Strong data-handling, validation and reconciliation skills with high attention to accuracy.
Proficiency in data analysis and reporting tools (advanced Excel essential; SQL, Power BI or similar advantageous).
Ability to identify, investigate and resolve data exceptions and anomalies.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to turn data into insight.
Disciplined, deadline-driven approach to recurring reconciliations and reporting.
Clear communication skills for reporting findings to internal and customer stakeholders.
Relevant tertiary qualification in data science, statistics, engineering, finance or a related quantitative field.
Preferable
Understanding of mining operations, fleet, fuel or asset data advantageous.
Outcomes and Deliverables
Deliverables
Daily and periodic data collection, compilation and validation completed to schedule.
On-time, accurate reconciliations with documented exception management.
Regular analytics outputs, trend reports and insight summaries for customers and internal stakeholders.
Exception and anomaly registers with resolution tracking.
Maintained data-process and control documentation for audit readiness.
Escalation reports on material issues to the Senior Manager.
Outcomes
Accurate, validated data consistently underpinning the contracted analytics services.
Reconciliations completed on time, every cycle, with no material errors.
Exceptions identified, managed and resolved promptly, with clear escalation of material issues.
Meaningful trends identified, managed and reported to support customer decisions.
Analytics service delivery meeting SLA, accuracy and timeliness commitments.
High customer confidence in the integrity of the analytics underpinning their solutions.

Job Description:
We are seeking a warm, experienced and professionally qualified Teaching Assistant/Learning Support Assistant to support an 8-year-old Grade 2 girl with classroom learning, concentration, organisation, homework, reading and revision.
The ideal candidate will be nurturing, patient, structured and passionate about education, with experience working with young children.
Key Responsibilities:
At School:
Attend school with the child and work alongside her during the school day.
Support her in understanding and completing classroom activities and instructions.
Reinforce concepts taught by the class teacher.
Assist with reading, writing, spelling, mathematics and other Grade 2 subjects where appropriate.
Help maintain concentration, organisation and positive classroom habits.
Assist with classwork when requested by the teacher.
Encourage independence rather than completing work on the child’s behalf.
Monitor areas where additional support or revision may be beneficial.
Communicate appropriately and professionally with the class teacher and parents.
Help keep track of homework, projects, assessments and important school requirements.
Afternoon Support:
Assist with daily homework.
Provide additional revision and consolidation of schoolwork.
Support reading practice and comprehension.
Assist with spelling, times tables and other age-appropriate foundational skills.
Prepare additional learning activities where beneficial.
Help the child develop good study habits and independence.
Assist with preparation for tests and assessments.
Encourage curiosity, confidence and a positive attitude towards learning.
Additional Responsibilities:
The successful candidate may also assist with:
Keeping school books, stationery and learning materials organised.
Preparing school bags and ensuring homework and projects are completed.
Encouraging good time management and responsibility.
Supporting the child’s participation in school activities where appropriate.
Providing occasional educational support during school holidays.
Liaising with parents regarding academic progress and areas requiring attention.
Identifying potential learning difficulties or areas of concern and communicating these to the parents and relevant educators — without attempting to diagnose them.
Qualifications & Experience:
A recognised teaching qualification / teaching degree.
Previous professional experience working with young children, preferably Foundation Phase / Grade 1–3.
Experience as a full-time teaching assistant, learning support assistant, classroom assistant or similar educational role.
Strong understanding of early primary school education.
Excellent English communication skills.
Ability to work professionally and collaboratively with teachers and parents.
Valid first-aid qualification would be advantageous.
A clear background check / police clearance will be required.
Advantageous:
Foundation Phase teaching experience.
Experience working within a Cambridge, IEB or similar primary-school environment.
Experience providing one-on-one academic support.
Knowledge of different learning styles and age-appropriate teaching techniques.
Experience helping children prepare for assessments.
Additional qualifications in child development, educational psychology, learning support or special educational needs would be beneficial.
The ideal candidate:
The ideal person will be someone who can become a positive and consistent educational mentor for the child.
We are not simply looking for someone to sit next to her and help her complete her work. We are looking for an experienced educator who can understand how she learns, identify where she needs support, reinforce what is being taught at school and help her develop strong foundations and confidence.
The successful candidate should be comfortable taking initiative, communicating with the child’s teachers and parents, and creating engaging ways to make learning enjoyable.
